newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London firm after Hang Seng surge.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London firm after Hang Seng surge.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks trading in London were higher across the board on Thursday with most interest focused in property stocks after a surge in the sector propelled the Hang Seng sharply higher to a record high.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was up 51.95 points at 16,417.66 by 1400 GMT.
"It really is just the property sector that is leading the way," said one London trader. "It stands out massively but everything else is firm on the back of this."

In Hong Kong on Thursday, property stocks were back in vogue on hopes of strong earnings growth on the back of rising sales. The Hang Seng surged 2.39 percent or 382 points to a record high of 16,365.71 whilst the property sub-index climbed four percent.
"Now we've consolidated above the 16,000 level there's more to come," said the trader. "I think we'll push on up...volumes have been very high, back up to pre-handover levels."

Among individual share features Cheung Kong was trading at HK$86.625, up from a Hong Kong close of HK$86. Sun Hung Kai Properties was quoted at HK$97.375 compared with a close of HK$97.250. Swire Pacific was up HK$3.52 at HK$73.55 after a Hong Kong close of HK$73.5.

Elsewhere, HongKong & Shanghai Banking Corp helped lift the broader market on the back of positive sentiment in London as the interim results season gets underway. HSBC Holdings was trading at HK$271.25 after a close of HK$270 and ahead of earnings next week.
